questions.q: Per this lesson, what are the three parts of a complete data model documentation package?
options: An ERD with legend, an object inventory table, and field-level notes
A sequence diagram, a DFD, and a system context diagram
A business requirements document, a budget estimate, and a timeline
An executive summary, an SDD, and an ADR
questions.explain: A complete data model package pairs the ERD (with legend, from Lesson 8) with an object inventory table describing each object's purpose and relationships, and field-level notes explaining non-obvious choices the diagram itself can't carry.

questions.q: What does the object inventory table add that the ERD diagram alone does not provide?
options: The exact cardinality of every relationship, duplicating the ERD
A plain-word statement of each object's purpose, giving a reader a single scannable reference instead of inferring purpose from object and field names
The Apex code implementing each object's triggers
The page layout assigned to each object
questions.explain: An ERD's boxes show structure and relationships; the object inventory table states what each object is actually for in plain words, which a diagram's shapes and lines don't communicate on their own.

questions.q: In this lesson's Task__c example, why was a lookup relationship to Project__c chosen instead of master-detail?
options: Because lookups are always the default choice regardless of business need
Because master-detail relationships are not supported on custom objects

Because Tasks should survive if a Project is deleted and re-created, since historical time entries on the Task matter for billing even after the Project wrapper is gone — master-detail's cascading delete would destroy that history
Because Task__c has no relationship to Project__c at all
questions.explain: The field-level note explains the reasoning: a Task's billing history needs to survive a Project being deleted and recreated, so a lookup (no cascading delete) was the deliberate, reasoned choice — not a default habit.

questions.q: Why does the junction object Project_Skill__c use master-detail relationships to both of its parent objects, per this lesson's reasoning?
options: Because junction objects are required to use lookup relationships, never master-detail
Because master-detail relationships prevent roll-up summary fields from functioning
Because Project_Skill__c is a standard Salesforce object
Because the junction record has no independent meaning without both parents, so it should logically cease to exist (cascading delete) if either parent is deleted
questions.explain: Unlike the Task__c case, a junction record's whole purpose is linking its two parents — if either parent disappears, the junction record no longer means anything, so cascading delete via master-detail is the correct behavior here.

questions.q: What underlying question does this lesson say should actually drive the choice between lookup and master-detail, rather than a fixed rule of thumb?
options: What should happen to the child record if the parent is deleted — should it be destroyed along with the parent, or should it survive?
Which relationship type requires less configuration effort
Which relationship type is alphabetically first in Setup
Whether the object is standard or custom
questions.explain: The lesson shows two relationships reaching opposite conclusions (lookup to preserve history vs. master-detail to enforce dependent existence) using the same reasoning skill: asking what should happen on delete and letting the real business answer decide.
